findings.text: Public suspend timing uses a dedicated suspend reference when present and reports no elapsed time otherwise, with distinct handling when the sampled source is itself that reference.
Suspend and resume visit registered sources in opposite orders invoking optional per source hooks, with resume also requesting watchdog reference renewal.
Registration establishes conversion and deferment limits, validates identity and user space acceleration mode, then enqueues the source for selection and supervision under global serialization.
Managed registration couples normal registration with automatic unregistration on device release.
Local timer arming rejects already pending timers and pins the timer to the current processor before scheduling.

Boot completion fixes the current source to the default, marks boot finished, performs an initial stability sweep and triggers selection, with the default provided by a weakly overridable low resolution source.
Published helper derives safe idle limits from conversion parameters and counter width, optionally returning the cycle bound.
Selection entry delegates to a shared selector in non forced mode.
Remote verification timeout is a fixed default on single node systems and otherwise grows with inter node distance up to a configured ceiling.

Frequency validation tolerates larger deviation for uncalibrated sources than when both reference and candidate claim calibration, rejecting samples whose reference readout window exceeds a bound within a bounded retry count.

Initial or explicitly reset validation establishes reference stamps without judging stability, while later samples compare interval deltas against idle limits and proportional allowance plus readout cost.
Inter processor validation cycles through online processors, never targets the local processor, and is bypassed for global test sources lacking per processor mode.

High resolution eligibility requires continuity of both candidate and reference, is deferred until boot completes, never applies to test sources, and triggers reselection or tick notification on change.
Maximum frequency correction is eleven percent of the base multiplier.
Advertised idle limit is one half of the computed overflow safe bound, and the negative motion threshold covers seven eighths of the counter range.
Suspend interval is reported only on forward progress of the suspend reference, with backward or equal readings yielding zero, and the reference disabled after use unless it is the current source.

Current source query and update plus available listing operate under global serialization, with available output omitting sources lacking high resolution eligibility while one shot tick mode is active.
Unbinding by name searches the registered list under global serialization and reports missing names without effect.

Watchdog enrollment either links verification required sources into a supervised list and clears their validated mark or, in reduced builds, only records high resolution eligibility for continuous sources.

Multiplier derivation from frequency uses a target interval derived from counter width and rate, clamped to at least one and at most six hundred, with iterative reduction to preserve headroom for adjustment.
Boot time source override stores a name for later selection under global serialization, with a legacy timer name mapped to its modern equivalent and warnings for old options.

Validation outcomes distinguish success, transient timeout or reset requiring retry, and persistent skew requiring instability marking, with remote timeouts logged once and frequency timeouts invalidating reference stamps.

Periodic supervision skips unstable entries while requesting background remediation after boot, applies frequency validation before inter processor validation, clears pending reset only after visiting all entries, and rearms by a fixed interval when not already pending.
Background remediation removes unstable entries, drops their rating, clears reselect requests, evaluates whether the supervision timer should stop, and reports whether fresh selection is needed.
Reference renewal on resume and explicit touch records a pending reset in full builds and does nothing in reduced builds, with the pending indication cleared only after a complete supervision walk.
Reduced builds provide inert supervision helpers that report no selection needed and perform no instability marking.
Global validation outcome and timestamp copies are protected by a raw spinlock taken with interrupts masked, while reference sampling uses interrupt masking alone.
The supervised list and running state are serialized by a dedicated spinlock held across the timer walk and the remediation sweep, with interrupt state preserved in the sweep.
A global mutex serializes registration, selection, boot completion, sysfs access, boot override storage and the remediation thread body.
Remote validation is single flight per target through a sequence flag and an in progress indicator plus a call lock, with concurrent attempts reported as timeout without issuing a new call.
The subsystem exposes three attributes for current selection, unbinding and listing, terminated by a null entry.
The subsystem registers a bus named for clock sources with a matching device name, and a single indexed device attached to that bus with associated attribute groups.

Observed sources carry identity and rating, mode and capability flags, counter width and conversion parameters with adjustment bounds, idle and cycle limits plus raw delta threshold, reference stamps, lifecycle and tick hooks, and list links for global and watchdog membership.

Sources requiring verification enter supervision unvalidated, become validated on first good sample, return to unvalidated on reference timeout or explicit reset, and move to unstable with rating loss and removal on persistent skew followed by reselection.

Before boot completion high resolution marking and background remediation are deferred, while completion fixes the current source, marks boot done, sweeps once and selects, thereafter enabling work scheduling and tick notification.
Power transitions traverse sources in reverse order on suspend and forward order on resume, with resume additionally requesting watchdog reference renewal.
Remote validation starts idle, moves to in progress when kicked, then resolves to success, skewed or timeout, with timeout leaving the target for a later cycle and skew forcing instability.
Timer expiry drives the periodic supervision walk and conditional rearm.
Dedicated thread context performs rating demotion and list pruning under locks then triggers selection if needed.
User and boot control arrives via handlers for current, available and unbind plus early boot parameter handlers and subsystem initialization.
Power management invokes suspend and resume hooks plus suspend interval start and stop helpers around the sleep interval.
A stale or concurrent remote request must not issue a second call, with busy targets treated as timeout to avoid interference.
Large multipliers combined with adjustment or long idle sleeps risk wide integer overflow, mitigated by shrinking conversion parameters, capping by counter width and halving the advertised limit.

Invalid identity values, missing frequency with coupled event requirements, and out of range acceleration modes are contained by clamping, flag clearing or disabling the affected feature with warnings.
Arming an already pending local timer is rejected with a one time warning and no state change.
Failure to enable the suspend reference aborts interval start with a one time warning, leaving prior state untouched.
High resolution threshold is one nanosecond.
Timer queue membership is represented as false for inactive and true for enqueued.
Active set is split into hard and soft partitions by a shift equal to the soft monotonic base, with hard covering lower bits, soft covering shifted bits and the union covering all.
